prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal]
Low poly 3D wallpaper of the attached print, plus `result.json` recording what was taken from it.

[action]
- Read `print.jpg`: Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" (title cartouche 冨嶽三十六景 神奈川沖浪裏).
- Built `scene/index.html`: one file, all geometry in code, no image textures. It loads only three@0.170.0 from the jsdelivr URL and one Google Font, with local serif fallbacks.
- Wrote `result.json`: `{"boats": 3, "mountain": "Mount Fuji"}`.
- Rendered it once in headless Edge at 1280x860 and compared the screenshot with the print.
- After that render I flipped the left boat, which sloped the wrong way (bow now high at left, as in the print).

[result]
- The render matched the print's layout: great wave curling from the left with foam claws, small snow-capped Fuji in the trough right of centre, three tan boats with indigo rowers, striped swell rising off the right edge, white foreground mound echoing Fuji, cartouche top left.
- Palette is Prussian blue, pale blue, cream foam, paper sky with a dark band at the horizon.
- Evidence: the render-check hook reported "0 console errors" on the final file. The left-boat fix itself was not re-screenshotted.
- Motion is by code only, not watched live: swell on all wave meshes, swaying foam, rocking boats, falling spray, slow camera drift with pointer parallax, damped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Boat count is from the image: one under the great wave at left, one in front of Fuji, one at lower centre.
- Known gap: the sky gradient shows blocky facets near the horizon, and the cloud is larger and more solid than the print's faint one.

Assumptions:
- "Wallpaper" means full-viewport and cover-fit to the print's 1280x860 frame, so very wide or tall windows crop the edges.
- The cartouche is HTML text, not 3D geometry.
- The signature line beside it is my approximate reading, not verified against the print.

[next]
Nothing owed. No browser windows remain open (the headless Edge run exited). Scratch screenshot and browser profile are in `./tmp`.
